_comment_tools: opencode scopes agents with a permission map (allow/ask/deny; the boolean `tools` map is deprecated), so tools_style permission-map renders '*': deny plus explicit allows. tool_map values are opencode permission keys; `list` rides the search capability because glob-style discovery is what that capability means on this runner.
_comment_models: Runner-specific spellings of the registry bindings (registry/models.yaml is the authority for WHICH model each role gets), in opencode's provider/model-id form from its Models.dev catalog. Open-weight POC (2026-07-23): all five models below are routed through the OpenRouter provider (one OPENROUTER_API_KEY covers every lab) as `openrouter/<org>/<model>` — opencode splits on the first '/' only, so the rest of the id passes through to OpenRouter. Any-provider harness: model_overrides implement the P5 vendor pins, and here implementer/reviewer/verifier land on three DISTINCT labs (DeepSeek / Moonshot / MiniMax) rather than just reviewer+verifier avoiding implementer's vendor — real three-way decorrelation, not the single-axis pin the claude-code and illustrative copilot-cli bindings settle for. Chosen for open-weight frontier capability at low cost as of 2026-07-23; re-verify pricing/availability before relying on this for anything beyond a POC, same as any registry/manifest binding.

_comment_model_vendors: Vendor of each runner spelling above, for the orchestrator's dispatch-time P5 check (avoid_vendor_of). Vendor is the underlying model lab, not the OpenRouter routing layer they're all fetched through — that's what P5 decorrelation actually means to guard (independent training/RLHF blind spots), and it's what the router's adapterVendor() keys on.
_comment_mode: mode: all lets a rendered agent be dispatched directly (`opencode run --agent <role>`) and invoked as a subagent; the rendered permission map is the ceiling either way.
_comment_headless: v1 orchestrator dispatch (docs/ORCHESTRATOR.md §5). --agent selects the rendered agent, whose frontmatter (incl. model_overrides above) pins the model. --auto is what makes runs unattended: it auto-approves ask-level permission prompts and honors deny, and the rendered maps only contain allow/deny, so nothing is silently widened. usage_report format ndjson-sum (verified live 2026-07-23): `opencode run --format json` streams one JSON event per line, one `step_finish` per agent turn (tool-using dispatches emit several), each carrying that turn's own cost/tokens rather than a running total — a live 2-tool-call probe produced two step_finish events summing to real cost, versus the old single-line-scan static-estimate fallback which either ignored usage entirely or would have picked up only the last turn (undercounting ~75% in that probe). line_filter selects step_finish lines; fields are dotted paths into each matching event.

headless._comment_resume: Same-round retry resume (#181). Every `--format json` event opencode emits carries the session it belongs to at the top level (`{type, timestamp, sessionID, ...}`), so session_field reads it off any line; the seam records it on the dispatch's ledger entry, and a retry of the same role+task+round passes resume_args to continue that session instead of re-deriving the whole exploration from nothing. `-s/--session <id>` is 'session id to continue' (verified against `opencode run --help`, v1.18.5); `--continue` is the no-id sibling ('continue the last session') and is redundant when an id is given. A session opencode no longer holds exits 1 with 'Session not found' and no JSON — the seam reads that as a refused resume and re-dispatches fresh.
